               <ns0:p n="2">2 To whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">By which tything to him, <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> owns him to be God's Priest. As he had received blessing from God by him, so he returns to God, through him, his Acknowledgments, he di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vided, shared, and gave out his part to him, even <ns0:hi>the tenth part of all the Spoils,</ns0:hi> v. 4. This is the first Scripture, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 14.20. that gives us any account of paying the <ns0:hi>Tenths</ns0:hi> of Goods to God in his Priests; which Custom afterwards obtained a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mong most Nations, to give the Tenths of the Spoils after Victory to God. And this <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> did, as due to the Office by divine Institution, having received a Blessing from it.</ns0:note>: first being by interpretation King of righteousness <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">The Mystery of his Name, Title and Descent, the Holy Ghost now opens to them. His Name is a compound of <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> or <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
which signifieth a <ns0:hi>King</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Governour,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>my King,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:hi>Righteousness.</ns0:hi> A supreme Governour, not only formally righ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teous in his own Disposition, but efficiently by just and excellent Laws making his Subjects righteous; a King working Righ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teousness in a <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> and in such a time of universal Degene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />racy from it. This God ordered for some special use, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> to type out his own Son, <ns0:hi>God-Man,</ns0:hi> the great Gospel-Mini<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ster to be the <ns0:hi>King of Righteousness,</ns0:hi> who purchased it for, im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />puteth it to, and infuseth it into Sinners; who is so fully the <ns0:hi>Lord our Righteousness,</ns0:hi> that we are made the Righteousness of God in him, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 32.1. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 23.6. and 33.16. <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 9.9. and 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 5.21.</ns0:note>, and after that also King of Salem, which is King of peace <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The Mystery of his Title of Office, <ns0:hi>King of Salem</ns0:hi>: The due order of this is observable; he is first, <ns0:hi>King of Righteousness,</ns0:hi> and after that he is <ns0:hi>King of Salem,</ns0:hi> that is, of Peace; the Fruit of whose righteous Government was Peace. He kept this among his People, and round a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bout him, while others were wasting and destroying their Kingdoms by Lusts and Wars. This is eminently true of Christ <ns0:hi>The Prince of Peace.</ns0:hi> Isai. 9.6, 7. who gave some signal of his Government, and begun his <ns0:hi>Priesthood</ns0:hi> in the same <ns0:hi>Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lem</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> where <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi> reigned, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 21.5, 9, 10. He is eminently the Royal Purchaser, Maker, and Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stributer of Peace, reconciling all things to God, Angels and Men in Heaven and in Earth, and all Persons, <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> and the Creation it self to recovered Man, <ns0:hi>Colos.</ns0:hi> 1.20, 21. comp. <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 2.13, to 18. The Prince and Price of our Peace, setting Peace within Souls, giving it to them with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out, Peace, spiritual, temporal, and eternal; his Kingdom aboundeth in it, <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 72.1, 3, 7. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 54.10, 13. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 14.27. <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> 3.18.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:555" />3 Without father <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">In this Verse is a mystical Description of the <ns0:hi>Eternity</ns0:hi> of Christ's <ns0:hi>Person</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Priesthood,</ns0:hi> set out by the Spirit in the Si<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lence and Omission of things that concerned <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi> and his Glory; so that what here is represented to be <ns0:hi>typically</ns0:hi> and in <ns0:hi>shadow,</ns0:hi> that was Christ <ns0:hi>really</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>substantially</ns0:hi>; for he gives no account of his Father, Mother, Genealogy, Birth, or Death; the Spirit either not revealing it to him, or or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dering him to leave it out, that he might appear the more lively and perfect Type of Christ, being represented in all things different from all the Men that ever were, or shall be; such a Priest therefore as he was, was Christ to be: Not de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riving his Priesthood from any by Birth, nor leaving it to any after him. As <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>without Father,</ns0:hi> that was a Priest before him, or is recorded from whom he should de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rive, as the Levitical Priesthood had; so Christ as to his <ns0:hi>Hu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manity,</ns0:hi> was without any Human Father, conceived only by the Power of the Holy Ghost.</ns0:note>, without mother <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">As to any Scripture-Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cords of it, or to any Title of the Priesthood by her, as those of <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s Family had: So Christ, as to his <ns0:hi>Deity,</ns0:hi> was without <ns0:hi>a Mother,</ns0:hi> being the eternal Son of the Father only, and without any Title in his <ns0:hi>Humanity</ns0:hi> to the Priesthood from the Virgin, she being of <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s Family, and not of <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>without pedigree.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out descent <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">There is <ns0:hi>no Line of him described</ns0:hi> in the Scripture, mentioning from whence he descended, or by what Genealogy he came to the Priesthood, as the <ns0:hi>Aaronites</ns0:hi> did clear their Right, <ns0:hi>Nehem.</ns0:hi> 7.64. As to Christ, who shall declare <ns0:hi>his Generation,</ns0:hi> or produce the lineal Role by which he claimeth the Priest<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hood? <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 53.8. comp. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 12, 15.</ns0:note>, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">There is no Record of his Birth or Death, tho he had a Father or Mother, as there is of <ns0:hi>Adam</ns0:hi>'s beginning and end, who had neither: So Christ as to his Priesthood had no Predecessor, nor shall have any Successor, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 16, 24, 28. As a Sacrifice and the Lamb of God, he had his time of entrance into the World, and of his leaving it; yet as God's <ns0:hi>Priest, he <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ad neither beginning nor end of days.</ns0:hi> Pure Eternity is its rise, and its end shall not be till God be all in all.</ns0:note>; but made like unto the Son of God <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, he was in these things the <ns0:hi>Shadow, Picture,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Resemblance</ns0:hi> of what Christ should be in his Royal Priesthood. In these singular Prerogatives a visible Type of <ns0:hi>God-Man</ns0:hi>; he was the Sign likening, and Christ was the Truth and Substance of it.</ns0:note>, abideth a priest continually <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">These Words, the Key to all the Description before. God made many other Persons eminent Types of his Son, but <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi> was the <ns0:hi>only Type</ns0:hi> of the Eternity of his <ns0:hi>Royal Priesthood</ns0:hi>; for which the Holy Ghost singled him out, dropt him down, as it were, from above, and then took him up again, without any further account of him in the Scripture, that he might convey this Mystery to us. That which hath no beginning nor end of it recorded, is as abiding for ever; which this Type had not; and so fully sets out the Truth designed to be conveyed by it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 Now consider how great this man <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">The Spirit compares with, and prefers <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi> be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> as he was God's High Priest; he introduces it with pressing these Hebrews to exercise an act of Judgment under the Metaphor of <ns0:hi>seeing,</ns0:hi> denoting it to be such a seri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous and intent act, as calls for the utmost Exercise of the discerning Faculty; a Carelesness in it, or an Oversight might make the Proposal to be to no purpose. The <ns0:hi>Greatness</ns0:hi> of this High-Priest is what he sets in their View, and that indefinitely, <ns0:hi>How great is this Officer</ns0:hi>? intimating him to be somewhat ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cessive to other great ones; and how much <ns0:hi>greater</ns0:hi> then must be <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> if his Type be so great beyond, not only <ns0:hi>Abraham, Levi,</ns0:hi> and his Posterity, but this great <ns0:hi>Melchisedec,</ns0:hi> as to his Sacerdotal Power and Dignity.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 14.20.</ns0:note> unto whom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">This Greatness is evinced by <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi>'s (the Patriarch, chief of all the Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> whom the Hebrews esteemed above all o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 8.53. and God owns as his Friend, and sets all Believers under his Fatherhood) giving, as a due to <ns0:hi>Melchise<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dec,</ns0:hi> being the greater Person in Office, the Tenth of all the Spoils, that which was due to God, and paid to him as God's High Priest; <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> notes either <ns0:hi>the first or choisest of the heaps of Grains,</ns0:hi> especially the first-Fruits dedicated to God; but here signifieth that part of the Spoils, which, according to the custom of War in most Nations after the Victory, were offered to God as his part; whether they did consist of Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons or Things; the tenth part of these were given by him to <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi> as the greatest Priest of God in the World, and superior to himself.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 And verily they that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the office of the priesthood <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">This is a Proof, by instance out of the <ns0:hi>Levitical Law,</ns0:hi> That he who receiveth is greater than he who giveth. The Seed of <ns0:hi>Levi</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> Son of <ns0:hi>Isaac,</ns0:hi> Son of <ns0:hi>Abra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ham,</ns0:hi> Numb. 1.48, 50. and 3.1, to 5. and not all of them neither, but the Sons of <ns0:hi>Levi</ns0:hi> descending from <ns0:hi>Aaron,</ns0:hi> were separated and consecrated in the Priesthood by God's Precept, and vindicated from those who would usurp it, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> ch. 16, and 17. and confirmed in it by Miracle.</ns0:note>, have a commandment to take tithes of the peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple according to the law <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">God himself gave them a Law from Heaven <ns0:hi>to tithe</ns0:hi> by, and a Charge to ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />serve this Law, as to all parts of Tithes, such as were due to all <ns0:hi>Levites</ns0:hi> Numb. 18.24. to the High-Priest only as God's Substitute, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 18.8, to 19. and 25. to 30. to the <ns0:hi>Levites</ns0:hi> Widows and Poor together, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 14.22, to 29. These the same Law obliged all the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> to pay to these <ns0:hi>Le<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vites</ns0:hi> as a Homage due from them to God, and so delivered to his Substitutes superior unto them as his Priests and Mini<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sters, and due to them by his own Constitution, being the first-Fruits of his own Blessing.</ns0:note>, that is, of their bre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thren, though they come out of the loins of A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />braham <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Yet these <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> who were to pay those Tithes to these as superior to them in Office, were <ns0:hi>their own Brethren</ns0:hi> by Nature, of the same Rank, coming out of the same Loins of <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> but subjected to these Priests, who, by God's Ordinance, were set above them in their Office; and their receiving Tithes, was an inseparable Property of the Superiority.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 But he whose <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>without pedegree.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> descent is not counted from them <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">The Proof is here applied, shewing <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi> to be greater not than the Levitical Priest only, but than <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> himself. He drew not his Genealogy from any Priests before him, but is greater than those Priests, who by Genealogy and Suc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cession were made such, and set above their Brethren by God himself: He being independent, having no Progenitor, Priest, or Successor, is greater than whom he decimateth.</ns0:note>, received tithes of Abraham, and bles<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 4.13. Gal. 3.16.</ns0:note> him that had the promises <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">He <ns0:hi>decimated Abraham</ns0:hi> the Father of the Levitical Priests, and by the most High's Order blessed him, by assuring him of his Peace with God, Grace continually from him, and mul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiplying temporal and spiritual Blessings to him, according as God promised, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 15.1, &c. And this he did to him, tho <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> was a Patriarch, and priviledged with Promises above any other, yet tho God were made over to him in all his fulness, the Blessing given him of Fatherhood to a nu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />merous Nation, even the visible Church of God among <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> as to all believing Gentiles, who had <ns0:hi>Canaan</ns0:hi> literally pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mised to his Posterity, and even this <ns0:hi>Salem,</ns0:hi> among the rest, of which <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi> was King, and the heavenly <ns0:hi>Canaan</ns0:hi> to himself; and above all, the promised <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> to descend from him, in whom himself and all Nations were to be blessed; he so great in Promises is tithed and blessed by a greater <ns0:hi>Melchisedec.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 And without all contradiction, the less is blessed of the better <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">This Principle is commonly acknowledged it is a most apparent Truth, you Hebrews cannot deny it; it is your com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon Judgment, That a <ns0:hi>Priest blessing, as God</ns0:hi>'s <ns0:hi>Officer, is greater than those blessed by him.</ns0:hi> He that is in a lower state in God's Church, is blessed by one set above him in Office by God himself, better and greater than he for his Place and Dig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nity in Office. He must have the preeminency for his Bles<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing, which he authoritatively, powerfully and effectually conveyeth from God to those he blesseth, representing there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in God communicating by him the good he wanteth in his Benediction.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 And here men that die <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">His greatness as to his Priesthood above the Levitical, is proved from its <ns0:hi>Immortality.</ns0:hi> Immortal is greater and bet<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter than Mortal; such is his Order of Priesthood. This Ar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gument he brings in to heighten the former, and so connects it to it. The Particle <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>here,</ns0:hi> if referred to <ns0:hi>time,</ns0:hi> notes du<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ring <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi>'s Oeconomy, while the Levitical Law lasted; if it refer <ns0:hi>to place,</ns0:hi> it notes <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> in the Land of <ns0:hi>Cana<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>n,</ns0:hi> where the Temple was, in that habitation of the <ns0:hi>Israelitish</ns0:hi> Church the Levitical Priests were not only as to their Nature and Persons withering and decaying, ceasing to be on Earth, tho they had the honour to decimate their Brethren, but as to their Order and Office <ns0:hi>Mortal,</ns0:hi> they were no better than the tithed and blessed by them, in <ns0:hi>prospect of Death. Aaron</ns0:hi> him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self the first of the Order died, and so did all his Successors as well as <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, receive tithes: but there he <ns0:hi>receiveth them,</ns0:hi> of whom it is wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nessed that he liveth <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">But how much better is <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi> and his Order? <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>there,</ns0:hi> may refer either to the place where his Business was transacted with <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> near <ns0:hi>Salem</ns0:hi>; or to the place of Scripture-record concerning him; either <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 14.18, 19, 20. where there is no account of his Death; or in <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 110.4. By the Prophet <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> is the Testimony born, that his Order is for ever; That <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi> as to his Order and Office of Priesthood now liveth and subsisteth in the Son of God incarnate, and continueth for ever. It is sug<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gested by a great Light in the Church, as if <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi> was translated as <ns0:hi>Enoch</ns0:hi> was, and so continued a Priest to the very Moment of his Translation; and that neither his Person nor Priesthood died, but liveth for ever: but in this the Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture is silent. Another refers it immediately to Christ, read<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing it thus; <ns0:hi>Here,</ns0:hi> i. e. in this World, <ns0:hi>they receive Tenths,</ns0:hi> or are Priests; but <ns0:hi>there,</ns0:hi> i. e. within the <ns0:hi>innermost of the Veil, whither the Forerunner is for us entred, Iesus:</ns0:hi> supplying this out of <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 6.19, 20. <ns0:hi>Here,</ns0:hi> is to be understood, not who re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceiveth Tithes, but <ns0:hi>who is,</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>whom it is witnessed that he liveth.</ns0:hi> He saith this Sense is to be found in so many words in <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 23, 24, 25. where <ns0:hi>those who receive Tenths, and die, v.</ns0:hi> 8. are no other Men than <ns0:hi>those many Priests who were not suffered to continue by reason of Death,</ns0:hi> v. 23. Nor <ns0:hi>he</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>whom it is wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nessed that he liveth,</ns0:hi> v. 8. can be any other than <ns0:hi>Iesus,</ns0:hi> who, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 24. is <ns0:hi>the Man that continueth for ever</ns0:hi>; and <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 25 <ns0:hi>is ever<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />living.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:555" />9 And as I may so say <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">The Spirit now sets this Priesthood above the Levitical by Instance, which Instance being not so proper or direct, his Form of introducing it, is considerable, as <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>as to say the Word,</ns0:hi> which is a <ns0:hi>Greek Elegancy of Speech,</ns0:hi> when that is uttered which is remarkable, and yet hard to be un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood; and it is not only <ns0:hi>conclusive</ns0:hi> to what was spoken before; <ns0:hi>I'le speak a word more,</ns0:hi> and then end the Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />course, but <ns0:hi>interpretative</ns0:hi> of what he was about to say con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> born 162 years after this Transaction; As <ns0:hi>I may so say,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>in some sense it may be said.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, Levi also <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> not so much taken <ns0:hi>personally</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>collectively</ns0:hi>; for the Tribe that sprung of him, who were Priests or Ministers to <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> which <ns0:hi>Levi</ns0:hi> personally was not. He was the third Son of <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> and his Seed God separated for, and consecrated to his Service, set<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ling the Priesthood in <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s Family, which was a Branch of that Tribe, and making all the rest Servants to them.</ns0:note>, who re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceived tithes, paid tithes in Abraham <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">These did receive these Tenths by God's Law from their Brethren, and these <ns0:hi>paid Tenths by,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>in Abraham,</ns0:hi> and so shewed them to be inferior in Office to <ns0:hi>Melchisedec,</ns0:hi> who re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceived this Homage from them as due to God, and to him as his High Priest. This was not properly, but figura<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tively; true Parents and Children being accounted here as one person before they exist, as well as after, <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> not actually existing then, but vertually in his Parent. <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> was in his Loins vertually too, as to his Humanity, but not to descend of him by natural Propagation, but by Miracle; and in <ns0:hi>him as an Antitype</ns0:hi> to this <ns0:hi>Melchisedec,</ns0:hi> and one to be set above him, in whom <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi> himself was to be blessed, and therefore could not pay Tenths to him in <ns0:hi>Abraham.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 For he was yet in the loins of his father when Melchisedec met him <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>For,</ns0:hi> introduceth the Proof, that <ns0:hi>Levi</ns0:hi> tithed in <ns0:hi>Abra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ham,</ns0:hi> being <ns0:hi>virtually in him,</ns0:hi> as his productive Cause; so near is the Unity and Identity of descending Children; <ns0:hi>and as truly were the Posterity of</ns0:hi> Adam <ns0:hi>in him when he ate, sinned, and fell,</ns0:hi> Rom. 5.12. To remove all question of the Truth of it, the time is annexed to it when <ns0:hi>Melchisedec met Abraham,</ns0:hi> and blessed him, then did <ns0:hi>Levi</ns0:hi> pay Tenths in him, so as <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi> was greater than the Levitical Priest; Christ typified by him being greater than himself, must be greater than them also.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gal. 2.21. v. 18, 19.</ns0:note> If therefore perfection were by the Le<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vitical priesthood <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Now the Spirit infers from the Doctrine of <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi>'s Priesthood, <ns0:hi>the dignity and perpetuity of Christ</ns0:hi>'s <ns0:hi>typified by it.</ns0:hi> So that it is not <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s Priesthood, but Christ's which the Hebrews were to use for their Salvation after <ns0:hi>Aaron's</ns0:hi> was ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pired. For <ns0:hi>Perfection</ns0:hi> was not to be had by <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s Priest<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hood or Law, but by a better, of another Order, even Christ and his Law. The form of these words are <ns0:hi>interro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gative,</ns0:hi> implying a vehement denial of what is queried in them. A <ns0:hi>perfecting</ns0:hi> of Persons to Life eternal by Expiation, Justification, Renovation, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> See <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 9.9. and 10.1. freeing Sinners from the Guilt, Stain, Filth, and Consequents of their Sins by an explatory satisfactory Sacrifice to God, and fitting of them for an eternal enjoying him: A <ns0:hi>Self-efficiency</ns0:hi> to these things without Christ, is as to the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> Priesthood vehe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hemently denied; as to this, that is defective.</ns0:note> (for under it the people re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceived the law <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">For with the Priesthood, about the time of its Institution by God, the <ns0:hi>Israelitish</ns0:hi> Church, God's covenanted People, <ns0:hi>received the Law</ns0:hi>; by which, as well as by its Priesthood, there is no Expia<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, Remission, nor eternal Life to be obtained, <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 3.17, 18, 19. comp. <ns0:hi>Mal.</ns0:hi> 2.4, to 8. This <ns0:hi>Law and Priesthood</ns0:hi> be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Types of far better to succeed them, they were but lead<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to them, which in the fulness of Time were to be re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vealed, and which should perfect what they could not, <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 3.23, 24. and 4.3, 4, 5.</ns0:note>) what further need <ns0:hi>was there</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">It was <ns0:hi>needful</ns0:hi> since the Leviti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cal Priesthood and Law could not perfect Sinners, that ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther should take place which could perfect them. <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> therefore, who lived above 400 years after their Institution, and feeling their Imperfection, did by the Spirit fore-see and tell of a <ns0:hi>Royal Priesthood and Law</ns0:hi> to take place after this, that should perfect Sinners, which could not be done by any called after <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s imperfect Order. This was the Lord Christ the Messiah, who must be after the Order of <ns0:hi>Melchi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sedec<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Psalm</ns0:hi> 110.4. and who by his Priesthood and Law should abundantly effect it; which was far more excellent for both, than any of the Levitical Family can pretend to.</ns0:note> that another priest should arise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 For the priesthood being changed <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>For,</ns0:hi> refers to the Expiration of the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> Order, to which these <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> now were not bound, for that a better Priesthood and Law were to fill up their room in the Church. The Levitical Priesthood was changed and abolish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed to make way for this; God designing that to continue for a time, and then to expire, when the Truth perfecting it should take place.</ns0:note>, there is made of necessity a change also of the law <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The mutation of the Priesthood indis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pensably requireth the <ns0:hi>change of the Law,</ns0:hi> i. e. <ns0:hi>the legal Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pensation of the Covenant of Grace,</ns0:hi> and the bringing in with another Priesthood a better Hope, <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 3.17, to 27. comp. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 18, 19 of this Chapter, even the Covenant of Grace in the Gospel-Dispensation of it. This was <ns0:hi>made necessary</ns0:hi> by the Decree of God, who determined, that both <ns0:hi>Priesthood</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Law</ns0:hi> should expire together, and accordingly hath ful<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />filled it. For when Christ the Gospel-High-Priest had in his Person and Work perfected all of it in Heaven, he roots out that Order of Priesthood, abolisheth the Law, scatters the People which would cleave to it; demolisheth the Temple and City to which he confined the Administration, so as all Designs and Endeavours of <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> or of apostate Christians, to repair, or to restore it, hath been ineffectual to this day.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 For he of whom these things are spoken, pertaineth to another tribe <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">That this Priesthood was so altered, he proves by Christ's being of another Tribe than <ns0:hi>Levi.</ns0:hi> This is a <ns0:hi>Periphrasis</ns0:hi> describing the Priest after <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi>'s Order. <ns0:hi>Of whom was this said</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 110.4. but of Ghrist, <ns0:hi>God-Man,</ns0:hi> the Royal High-Priest of God, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 21.42. He, as to his human Nature, descended of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> and not of <ns0:hi>Levi</ns0:hi>; and so the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> Priesthood was ended by him, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 2.14. <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 49.10.</ns0:note>, of which no man gave attendance at the altar <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Of which Tribe none was a Priest, whose work was to attend the Altar, and offer Sacrifice; if any of another Tribe pretended to, or would usurp it, God either smote them, as <ns0:hi>Vzziah,</ns0:hi> 2 Chron. 26.18. or destroyed them as those Rebels, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 16.1, 2, 4, 28, to 36. neither was the <ns0:hi>Priesthood</ns0:hi> hereby made <ns0:hi>tribual,</ns0:hi> or continued in any such Tribe as in <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> but confined to our Lord only, not because he descended of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> but extraordinarily selected of God out of it to discharge it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 For <ns0:hi>it is</ns0:hi> evident that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matth. 1.3.</ns0:note> our Lord sprang out of Judah <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The proof of this change of the Tribe, and of what Tribe he was, was undeniably evident to these Hebrews from their own Genealogies, and the <ns0:hi>Roman</ns0:hi> Cense and En<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rolement of him. The Providence of God ordering this, that it might be universally known that he was <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s Seed, as well as <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi>'s, and as called by his Name, <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 34.23, 24. and 37.24, 25. Our Lord was <ns0:hi>God-Man,</ns0:hi> Lord Mediator, <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 110.1, 4. <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 22.42, 46. He was, as to his Humanity, born of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> as his Ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nealogy by his Mother doth evince, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 3.33. and the concomitant evidence of the <ns0:hi>Roman</ns0:hi> Rols in which his Name was registered and kept in their Archives above an Age af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter his Ascension.</ns0:note>, of which Tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">No Man of which Tribe was so de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />signed by God, or so revealed to have the Royal Priesthood, but himself. None of them having any Right to it, as they could prove out of <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi>'s <ns0:hi>Writing</ns0:hi>; and the Rule of Priest<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hood is to be found there, and no where else: So that a negative Argument taken from Scripture in matters of Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ligion is valid, tho never so much puft at in this Age.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 And it is yet far more evident <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">The Change and Abolition of the Levitical Priesthood, and Law, that the perfecting one of Christ might succeed, is not only clearly represented to the understanding of all, that they assent to it, but it <ns0:hi>is far more evident</ns0:hi> from the Eternity of this Priesthood's Constitution, as is proved <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 16. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>if</ns0:hi> is a Particle vehemently asserting, as in form of swearing, and not doubting, and therefore rendered <ns0:hi>for that.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, for that <ns0:hi>p</ns0:hi> after the similitude <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Like</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Parallel</ns0:hi> in order to him, and in all the pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />perties foretold, which make him a most excellent Priest; a Priesthood far above that of <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi> upon the account of the Law and Covenant to which it is related, which was not only the Law of Nature, serving God as Creator, but the Law of Grace as he was Redeemer in Christ, who with the Pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />triarchs worshipped God by, as believed in a Christ to come.</ns0:note> of Melchisedec there ariseth another priest <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Not only of another Tribe than <ns0:hi>Aaron,</ns0:hi> but of a different Order from his, is constituted, manifested, and beginneth the Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ercise of his Office with the Abolition of <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:556" />16 Who is made, not after the law of a car<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal commandment <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">The Gospel-High-Priest the Lord Jesus Christ was not constituted, nor consecrated after that Order and Rule of God, which did bind the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> Priesthood, and regulate it as to their Consecrations and Ministrations, obliging them by annexed temporal Promises and Comminations which could not reach an immortal Soul. The Mosaical Rites and Ceremonies were bodily, fleshly, only external. He was not made a Priest by legal Purifying with Water, nor anointed with Oyl, nor sprinkled with Blood, nor clothed with Priestly Garments, as <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi> and his Order was, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> ch. 39, and 40.13, 14, 15, 31, 32. nor initiated with Sacrifices of Bulls, Goats, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> He was not to minister in a Taber<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nacle or Temple as they did, which was carnal, and reached only the Flesh, could not expiate Sins, nor procure spiri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tual and eternal Blessings, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 9.1, to 11, 12, 13, 19, to 27.</ns0:note>, but after the power of an endless life <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">But was constituted and consecrated by God accor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ding to his <ns0:hi>powerful Law.</ns0:hi> He was anointed with the Holy Ghost and Power, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 10.38. which mighty influence enabled him to execute his Office effectually for saving Sin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ners; and by it he receiveth <ns0:hi>Life</ns0:hi> peculiar to his Priesthood, opposed to the <ns0:hi>dead Letter</ns0:hi> of the Commandment, by which, and under which, Souls perished by multitudes. But this High-Priest hath by <ns0:hi>this Law life</ns0:hi> in himself, and the <ns0:hi>best of life</ns0:hi> to give out no those who wait on his Ministry, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 5.21, 24.25, 26. and such <ns0:hi>life as is indissoluble,</ns0:hi> opposite to carnal and bodily, which corrupts and perisheth; but the <ns0:hi>powerful life</ns0:hi> of this Priest is not to be destroyed, neither in himself, nor his People. He by his Death and Life makes eternal Expiation, and procureth eternal Blessings for them; See <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 25. and <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 9.11, 12, 28.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 For he testifieth <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">This is proved by infallible Testimony in <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 110.4. <ns0:hi>God the Father</ns0:hi> himself solemnly declared him to be so before the Angels in Heaven, and revealed it to Men on Earth by the Prophet <ns0:hi>David.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, Thou <ns0:hi>art</ns0:hi> a priest for ever, after the order of Melchisedec <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">That as <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi> had no end of Days recorded, so this is repeated again to prove, that the Priest after his Similitude, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> after his Order (the words being here synonimous) must continue for ever. Christ was not a temporary Priest by a carnal Law, but was made a Priest for ever, with everlasting power endowed to save all his People; See <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 24, 25, 28. and <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 1.21.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 For there is verily a disannulling of the com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mandment going before <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">The Spirit having proved the disannulling of the <ns0:hi>Aaro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nical</ns0:hi> Priesthood for its Imperfection, proceeds to prove the Abolishing of the Law or Covenant annexed to it, like it for weakness and unprofitableness; <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> is a <ns0:hi>displacing, depo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>laying it aside</ns0:hi> as to its binding force, so as there is no Obligation from it on any as to Obedience or Penalty; and this is so disannulled of the Law-maker, God himself, by setting up the Gospel by his Son Priest, which is most certainly true.</ns0:note>, for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gal. 4.9.</ns0:note> the weakness and unprofitableness thereof <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">For the <ns0:hi>Mosaical Covenant and Law</ns0:hi> wanted strength to bring about what the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> sought by it, and wanted good Fruit to them who made their boast of it, both which weakness and unprofitableness arose from the Hebrews abuse of it, expect<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Expiation and Sanctification by it, without minding the Promise which preceded it 430 years, to which it should have led them, and by its neglect proved so fatal to them. For they would be justified and saved by an external Obe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dience to this Law, without any regard to Christ and his Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifice, by whom alone it could be attained, <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 3.17, to 27. It was strong and profitable to the end for which God made it to lead to Christ, but weak and unprofitable to justi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fie or sanctifie them without him, which was the end they use it for, or rather abused it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Act. 13.36. Rom. 8.3. Gal. 2.19.</ns0:note> the law made nothing perfect <ns0:hi>z,</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>but it was the bringing in.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> but the bringing in of a better hope <ns0:hi>did</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>But,</ns0:hi> shews the opposition <ns0:hi>of Hope</ns0:hi> to the <ns0:hi>Law,</ns0:hi> tho the <ns0:hi>Law</ns0:hi> could not <ns0:hi>perfect</ns0:hi> any, yet the <ns0:hi>better Hope,</ns0:hi> the Gospel-Law, promulgated to, and received by them, could perfect them. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>Super<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />induction,</ns0:hi> i. e. it was brought in, and put in force after the legal Covenant expired, and brought in to abolish that, so as by it it was repealed and abrogated. The Gospel-Law is stiled <ns0:hi>a better Hope,</ns0:hi> because it is conveying better Promises, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 8.6. which give firm and certain Hope of Sinners Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fection by it, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> their Injoyment of Justification, Sanctifi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cation and eternal Life. This Hope wrought by the Holy Ghost in their Hearts, enableth them to obey the Gospel, and seals the Promises to them. And by this they</ns0:note>: by the which we draw nigh unto God <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">have <ns0:hi>free ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cess to God,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 4.14, 16. comp. <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 10.19, to 23. and <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 5.1, 2<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> not only to worship him, but to receive the Blessings of the Covenant from him, without fear of displeasing him, or being consumed by him, as under the Law, but in the great<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />est confidence of pleasing him in Jesus Christ, of having Communion with him, and of being blessed in the Enjoy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of him for ever; See <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 12, 18, to 22. and comp. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 22, to 25. with them.</ns0:note>
                  <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  <ns0:note place="bottom">The Proof of this weakness and unprofitableness of the Law is its <ns0:hi>Imperfection</ns0:hi>; it had no supernatural moral power to justifie or sanctifie any person, or to bring them to perfection; neither did it perfect any person of it self, so as to reconcile it to God, or bring it to Salvation whatever was expected by it, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 9.9. and 10.1, 2.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 And in as much as not without an oath <ns0:hi>he was made priest</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">This is a further Proof of the Excellency of Christ's Priesthood above <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s, taken from his <ns0:hi>Constitution in it by Oath.</ns0:hi> He who is made a Priest <ns0:hi>by Oath,</ns0:hi> is a better, and a greater Priest than any made so without it, but so is Christ. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
is a comparative, answered <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 22, insinuating <ns0:hi>by how much</ns0:hi> the Cause constituting or confirming an Office of Priest<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hood is more excellent, by <ns0:hi>so much</ns0:hi> the Effect and Office must excel, receiving greater Power for some more excellent end. This <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> is as much as a <ns0:hi>double Oath,</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. By <ns0:hi>the swearing of an Oath</ns0:hi> by God the Father was the Gospel-High-Priest constituted an eternal one after <ns0:hi>Melchise<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dec</ns0:hi>'s Order; and it addeth so much the more Strength and Glory to the Sanction. This is testified by <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> Psal. 110.4. The Levitical Priests were made by a divine Designation, and with external Rites were consecrated; but Christ was con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stituted a Priest by Oath, as our Translators well supply it out of the following Verse.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 (For those Priests were made <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>Without swearing of an Oath.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> without an oath <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Those Priests of <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s Order were selected, instituted, consecrated <ns0:hi>without any Oath</ns0:hi> mentioned by <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> who did all exactly as the Lord commanded him, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 40.16. God gave only command for it, and made their Priest<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hood but a temporary and passing Honour and Office, which he might alter when he would:</ns0:note>: but this with an oath, by him that said unto him, The Lord sware <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">But <ns0:hi>he,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Iesus,</ns0:hi> was made a Priest after <ns0:hi>Melchisedec</ns0:hi>'s Order, <ns0:hi>by an Oath</ns0:hi> of God his Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, speaking to him, as is recorded by <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> Psalm 110.4. The Lord <ns0:hi>Iehovah</ns0:hi> the Father, sware unto his Son the Lord <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> lifting his Hand, and saying, I live for ever, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 32.40. when he ascended and sate down on the Right Hand of the Majesty in the Heavens, solemnly by this Oath ratify<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing and confirming him in this Office, and that he <ns0:hi>would not repent,</ns0:hi> i. e. change, or alter, or retract what he swore to him, there being no need of any other, he so effectually perfor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ming the work of it, that all that God bestows upon his by him, are Gifts not to be repented of, even eternal Life and Salvation. That which the Oath ratified, was, That Christ should be God's only and eternal Priest, who was to have no Sharer with him in the Priesthood, and no end of it; ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />king away from himself by Oath any power to make Christ no Priest, or take away his Office at will and pleasure, as he did <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s; hereby honouring his Son, and highly gratifying Sinners by giving them such a Royal High-Priest, who should effectually manage all their Concernments with him for ever.</ns0:note>, and will not re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pent, Thou <ns0:hi>art</ns0:hi> a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.)</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 By so much was Jesus made a surety <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">This brings in the Consequent on <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 20. <ns0:hi>As much</ns0:hi> Excel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lency as was in God's Oath constituting, <ns0:hi>so much</ns0:hi> there must be in the Office constituted. The <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> Priesthood by God's Constitution, was excellent; but Christ's is much more so, being by God's Oath made personal and everlasting, re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lating to the best Covenant; so as the Hebrews had the greatest reason to renounce <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s, and to cleave to Christs for Salva<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion. He being <ns0:hi>God-Man,</ns0:hi> is a <ns0:hi>Surety,</ns0:hi> one <ns0:hi>that bindeth himself for another, to see something paid or performed, to give security for another</ns0:hi>; and is proper to him as a Priest, <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 17.3. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 119.122<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 6.1. In the Mosaical Oeconomy the Priests were <ns0:hi>typical Sureties,</ns0:hi> or Undertakers for the People; so <ns0:hi>Aaron,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>a Surety,</ns0:hi> was sent by <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> to stand between the Living and the Dead, when God was cutting off those Sinners, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 16.46, 48. The Spirit interprets this <ns0:hi>Surety,</ns0:hi> to be a Mediator, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 8.6. which is the general comprehensive Name of all his Offices; as he gives all from God to us in and by his Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mises, <ns0:hi>he is Testator</ns0:hi> fulfilling them, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 9.15, 16. As he gives satisfaction to God for us, and returns our Duty performed with the Incense of his Merits. He is our <ns0:hi>Surety</ns0:hi>; which merit of his resulted from his perfect Obedience to the whole Law and Will of God, and from the full Satisfaction he made to God by his Death for our Sins. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 5.19. 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 5.21. <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 3.13.</ns0:note> of a better testament <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Gospel-Covenant</ns0:hi> described, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 8.10, 11, 12. and referreth to what the Lord foretold of it, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 31.33, 34. which is <ns0:hi>better</ns0:hi> than the Mosaical for Perspicuity, Freeness, Fulness, Spirituality, and the Spirit promised in it for its Ratification by the Death of Christ and its Perpetuity; See <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 8.8, 9, 11.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:556" />23 And they truly were many priests <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">This further demonstrates the excellency of Christs Priesthood above the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> for its Singularity and Self-sufficiency; whereas theirs was for the Multiplicity of it, weak, vanishing, and mortal, like themselves: They <ns0:hi>had multitude of Priests</ns0:hi> together under the High Priest, to manage the Service, and above <ns0:hi>seventy High Priests</ns0:hi> beside their <ns0:hi>Sagans,</ns0:hi> such as were to officiate for them, if at any time they were legally disabled from the Institution of the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> Order, to the Destruction of the Temple, and were made according to the Law successively.</ns0:note>, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause they were not suffered to continue, by rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son of death <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Death</ns0:hi> cut them off one after another, they were all mortal, and could not abide neither in their Priesthood or Life, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 28.43. Death transmitted that Priesthood from one unto another; 'tis the Priesthood it self by the Succession of a better, was abolished, and did expire, so frail, passing, and imperfect was both their Persons and Office.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 But this <ns0:hi>man</ns0:hi> because he continueth ever <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>This Priest Iesus,</ns0:hi> v. 22. is opposed to the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> mul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />titude, this excellent one, 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.5. after his Resurrection abideth immortal. He is eternal and permanent for Person and Office; See <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 25. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 6.9. They are vanished, but he continues for ever, <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 1.17, 18.</ns0:note>, hath an <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>which <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> not from one <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> another.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> unchangeable priesthood <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, a Priest<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hood <ns0:hi>that cannot pass from him to any other,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s did to his Successors: No person is to be a Sharer in it, nor a Successor to it; it is reciprocal with himself; his individual Person terminateth it for ever; he hath no Vicars nor Suc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cessors of his Priesthood, whatever the Pope pretends to in it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 Wherefore he is able <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">This Inference proves his Eminency in Office above <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s Order by the Efficacy of it; for <ns0:hi>he is Possessor of a super<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />natural divine Power which is able to save</ns0:hi> to perfection, to the full, to all ends from Sin, in its Guilt, Stain and Power; from its Consequents, the Curse, and Wrath, and eternal Death. What neither our selves, nor others could do for us, he is <ns0:hi>only able,</ns0:hi> and as willing as able to set us in a safe, happy, blessed and glorious State for ever, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 5.9, 10, 11, 17.</ns0:note> also to save them to the <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>evermore.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> uttermost, that come unto God by him <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">All <ns0:hi>such who will come to God by him,</ns0:hi> as their High Priest, and no other, praying for Remission of Sins for his sake and merit, by Faith in his Blood, renouncing self, expecting the Mercy of God to flow in him to them, subjecting themselves en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tirely to him, and depending on him to present them unto God their end, without Spot or Blemish, or any such thing, and to make them blessed in the enjoyment of him for ever. This is his Work, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 6.35, to 41. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 3.18.</ns0:note>, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Since he always <ns0:hi>exists and lives an High Priest</ns0:hi> for the good of those who wait on him, having life in himself, and quick<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning them, comp. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.6. And as <ns0:hi>their Advocate,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn.</ns0:hi> 2.1, 2. answereth all Charges against them, suing for those penitent Believers, and pleading for all promised them by the Father in him. He sitting at God's Right-Hand must ever be in his presence, and appears as the ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neral Representative of his, and useth all his Interest with the Supreme Law-giver, Judge, and Governour, for them; See <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 9.24. as it was foretold he should, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 53.12. even <ns0:hi>for them</ns0:hi> who cannot plead their own Cause through Guilti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, or Weakness; he will manage it for all of them who believe in him, and apply themselves to God by him, at<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />toning him for their sins by his Sacrifice, perfuming Duties and Person by the Insence of his Merits, and presenting them to God, answering in Heaven his Type on Earth, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 30.1, to 10. comp. <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 8.3, 4. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.31, to 36.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 For such an high priest became us, <ns0:hi>who is</ns0:hi> holy <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">The last Excellency of the Gospel-High-Priest, prefer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ring him to <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s Order, is the <ns0:hi>Qualification of his Person,</ns0:hi> by which he is described in himself, distinguished from, and set above all others, and is that which remained out of <ns0:hi>Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid</ns0:hi>'s Proof to be cleared, who this Person was, who was different from <ns0:hi>Melchisedec,</ns0:hi> tho after his Order, to take place after <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s was expired, who was immortal, and constituted an everlasting Priest by God's Oath, This was God-Man, the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> and Gospel-High-Priest, who was <ns0:hi>convenient, con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gruous, sutable, use<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ul</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>necessary for us</ns0:hi> guilty, filthy, mise<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rable Sinners, in respect of our selves hopeless, and helpless, and cannot approach God without Consumption; and unless we have a Person who can manage our Cause with God, are lost for ever. To such is he agreeable and necessary, who can only help and save us. This the Titles given him, e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vince, shewing all the Perfections of a Priest, of which others were dark shadows and Types. As he was not only exter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nally and relatively by Office, but internally and morally <ns0:hi>holy.</ns0:hi> His Essence as God, was <ns0:hi>Holiness</ns0:hi>; as Man his Nature was intirely agreeable to God's Will; he was <ns0:hi>that holy thing,</ns0:hi> Luke 1.35. not having Holiness engraven on a Mitre, as <ns0:hi>Aaron,</ns0:hi> Exod. 39.30, 31. but in his Person; <ns0:hi>holy</ns0:hi> in his Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ception, Birth, Life and Death: The Devil could find no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing but Holiness in him, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 14.30. Pure in his Soul, in his Body transcendently beyond his Type, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 21.17, to 23. not a Creature, Angel or Man so holy as he, the most like to God of any, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.14.</ns0:note>, harmless <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>Void of all na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tural evil in his Spirit and Flesh,</ns0:hi> no Lust, no Disposition to evil, not injurious to any, having no Guile, an <ns0:hi>Israelite</ns0:hi> indeed beyond a <ns0:hi>Nathaniel</ns0:hi> of the most simple, pure, and innocent Nature; he was good, and all his Work was good, <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 10.38.</ns0:note>, undefiled <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>without any Spot,</ns0:hi> not soiled or stained without or within; the Angels and Heavens are not so clean in God's sight, as this Priest of his; he was never tainted with the Appearance of Sin: if his Church be so pure, what must himself be? <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 5.27.</ns0:note>, separate from sinners <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Free from all vicious habit, quality, Act or Stain,</ns0:hi> by what was in Sinners, or by his Converse with them; as separate from Guilt or Stain, as if he had never been with them; conjoyned with God in Being and Ful<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness of Righteousness, making Sinners righteous, but con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tracting nothing from them.</ns0:note>, and made higher than the heavens <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">By the Constitution of God after his Sacrifice mentioned <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 27. he ascended far above all Heavens, <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 4.10. and is setled on God's Throne at his Right-Hand, having all Principalities, Powers, Might and Dominion, and every Name subjected to him, and all things put under his Feet, <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 1.21, 22. Never Priest can reach where he is; this is his supereminent Excellency, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 4.14. and 8.1. and 9.11. How able, mighty and successful is he for managing all for his Clients there? His Work now is In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tercession.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 Who needeth not daily, as <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.3<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> those high priests, to offer up sacrifice <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">In this Verse the Spirit shews the ground of his Inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cession-work in Heaven, and why he doth not sacrifice as an High Priest there; therein setting His far above the <ns0:hi>Aaro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nical</ns0:hi> Priesthood. He had no necessity, being so holy as he was, to multiply Sacrifices either for himself being sinless, and had no Infirmity to atone for, as the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> Priest<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hood had, who annually on the day of Atonement did of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fer Sacrifice for themselves, being Sinners, and needed Par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />don as well as the People, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 9.7.</ns0:note>, first for his own sins, and then for the peoples <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">He had no need annually at a day to offer for the Peopl's sins, as <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi> and his Successors had, and did continue to do, till his Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifice took place and abolished them; he having once of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fered a Sacrifice for the sins of the People, which out-weigh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed all their multiplied Sacrifices; and this he did <ns0:hi>once when he himself died a Sacrifice for sins,</ns0:hi> when he offered up the hu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man Nature by the eternal Spirit without Spot, a propitiatory Sacrifice to God, when his Body hung on the Cross, and his Soul ascended and entred into the Throne of God in the Holy of Holiest in Heaven, with the Blood of the Te<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stament, and attoned him for all his People. How tran<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scendent was this Sacrifice to all the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> ones, where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />by Sinners were reconciled unto God for ever, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 9.11, 12, 14, 24, 25, 26. On this Offering was he exalted by God far above all Heavens, confirmed by Oath in his Office, and his Intercession became so powerful and effectual to save all his People from their sins, and the Consequents of them.</ns0:note>: For <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Chap. 10.12.</ns0:note> this he did once when he offered up himself <ns0:hi>x.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 For the law maketh <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 2.10. & 5.9.</ns0:note> men high priests which have infirmity <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">This is the Reason why the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> Priests had need to sacrifice for themselves, and the Gospel-High-Priest had not, and is finally describing him who is so. For the Law which God gave to <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> the Ceremonial Law, constituteth, sets up, and puts into this <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> Order and Office of Priest<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hood such as are not only liable to bodily <ns0:hi>Infirmities,</ns0:hi> but to moral ones, sins. <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi> and all his Sons, had their spiritual sinful Infirmities, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 5.2. for which they were to offer their propitiatory Sacrifices to God, as well as for those of the People, they were sinful dying Men, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 26.</ns0:note>, but the word of the oath which was since the law <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">But God the Father's Promise to his Son, ratified with an Oath, that he should be the great High-Priest perfecting of Souls for God, as <ns0:hi>Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid</ns0:hi> testifieth, <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 110.4. to be revealed to him; and this 400 years after the Law was given, which constituted the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> Priesthood. The <ns0:hi>Word</ns0:hi> revelead God's Promise to him, the <ns0:hi>Oath</ns0:hi> made it irreversible; yet this Promise was not actually performed to him till his Ascension in the human Nature higher than the Heavens, <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 110.1.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>maketh</ns0:hi> the Son, † who is <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>perfected.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> consecrated for evermore <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">God the Son incarnate, the Man Christ God's Fellow, the glorious only begotten and bosome Son of the Father, <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 13.7. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.14, 18. 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.5. is made by this ratified Word the only single everlasting High-Priest, who is not only compleatly and perfectly holy, as opposed to the Infirmities of the <ns0:hi>Aaroni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cal</ns0:hi> Priests, but ever able and fit for his Work, as succes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful in it. Who would not therefore leave that abolished Priesthood, and cleave to this which must abide for ever?</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
